title: Paired comparisons and clustered uncertainty
outcome: Compute paired and family-level uncertainty while distinguishing a randomization null, a bootstrap approximation and a deployment claim.

exercises.title: All differences vanish
exercises.hint: Every allowed statistic equals the observed statistic.
exercises.answer: There is no observed contrast. All sign assignments are at least as extreme under the non-strict tail convention.

exercises.title: Four favorable pairs
exercises.hint: Count both all-positive and all-negative assignments.
exercises.answer: Even four uniformly favorable pairs cannot attain a two-sided 0.05 threshold under this small sign space.

exercises.title: Reverse model labels
exercises.task: Negate every difference in case A.
exercises.answer: A two-sided sign-reference test does not favor a naming convention; a one-sided analysis would require a prespecified direction.

exercises.title: State the quantile convention
exercises.task: Compare linear interpolation with empirical inverse-CDF percentiles in case B.
exercises.expected: Linear endpoints are approximately +/-0.925; inverse-CDF endpoints are +/-1.
exercises.hint: A discrete bootstrap distribution needs an explicit quantile rule.
exercises.answer: Both calculations use the same four resamples. Different interpolation rules do not constitute additional evidence.

exercises.title: Add a third family
exercises.expected: There are 27 ordered draws of three families.
exercises.hint: Each of three positions has three choices.
exercises.answer: The calculation expands to 3 cubed assignments, while the original independent sample still has only three families.

exercises.title: Bound an exact algorithm
exercises.answer: A bounded classroom example should not silently allocate an enormous sign space. A larger analysis needs a declared Monte Carlo or analytical method.
